\chapter{Boolean Analysis — Invariance — Replacement}
%%% generated by the blueprint pipeline from TCSlib.BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.Replacement
\section{Overview}
Independent affine inputs can be integrated separately from a common background, yielding fourth-order scalar and single-coordinate replacement estimates.

\section{Declarations}

\begin{theorem}[Integrating an independent affine input]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.independent_affine_integral}
\leanok
\difficulty{5}
Let $A,D,W$ be real functions on a probability space $(\Omega,\mu)$ such that $(A,D)$ and $W$ are measurable up to null sets and $W$ is independent of $(A,D)$. If $\psi\colon\mathbb R\to\mathbb R$ is continuous and $\psi(A+DW)$ is integrable, then $q(a,d)=\mathbb E_\mu[\psi(a+dW)]$ is integrable under the law $\lambda$ of $(A,D)$ and $\mathbb E_\mu[\psi(A+DW)]=\int q(a,d)\,d\lambda(a,d)$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Replacement with a shared random background]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.independent_affine_replacement_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.affine_replacement_bound, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.independent_affine_integral, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.integrable_mul_pow_of_memLp}
\difficulty{5}
Let $A,D,U,V$ be real random variables on a probability space, with $A,D\in L^4$. Suppose each of $U,V$ is independent of the pair $(A,D)$ and is measurable up to a null set with finite fourth absolute moment, first three moments $0,1,0$, and fourth moment at most $9$. If $\psi\in C^4(\mathbb R)$, $C\ge0$ bounds $|\psi^{(4)}|$ everywhere, and both $\psi(A+DU)$ and $\psi(A+DV)$ are integrable, then $|\mathbb E\psi(A+DU)-\mathbb E\psi(A+DV)|\le(3C/4)\mathbb E[D^4]$.
\end{theorem}

\begin{theorem}[Error from replacing one polynomial input]
\lean{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.single_coordinate_replacement_bound}
\leanok
\uses{BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.HasInvarianceMoments, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.coordinateDerivative, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.coordinateDerivative_coeff, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.coordinateFree, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.eval_coordinate_split, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.Invariance.indep_coordinate_parts, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.independent_affine_replacement_bound, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.integrable_test_of_memLp_four, BooleanAnalysis.GaussianSpace.invariance_coordinate_fourth_moment, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.MultilinearMoments.eval_eq_of_off_coordinate, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV, BooleanAnalysis.Hypercontractivity.evalMultilinearRV_memLp, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.HasDegreeAtMost, BooleanAnalysis.ThresholdFunctions.MultilinearPolynomial.eval, BooleanAnalysis.influence}
\difficulty{5}
Let $F(x)=\sum_{S\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}}a_S\prod_{j\in S}x_j$ be a real multilinear polynomial and fix $i\in\{1,\ldots,n\}$. Suppose $F$ has degree at most $k+1$, and $X,Y$ are real input families on one probability space, each independent within itself, agreeing as functions at every coordinate other than $i$. Every input is measurable up to a null set with finite fourth absolute moment, first three moments $0,1,0$, and fourth moment at most $9$. If $\psi\in C^4(\mathbb R)$ and $C\ge0$ bounds $|\psi^{(4)}|$ everywhere, then $|\mathbb E\psi(F(X))-\mathbb E\psi(F(Y))|\le(C/12)9^{k+1} I_i(F)^2$, where $I_i(F)=\sum_{S\ni i}a_S^2$.
\end{theorem}
